answer: Each identity locks a 55-credit bond at the harbor registry and publishes one key-signed thread. A sparrow auditor groups threads by shared fragments, recomputing the grouping from the registry, so a copied thread cannot hide. Registration costs 20 credits plus 6 credits per earlier thread checked, so the kth fake pays 75 credits plus 6 credits for every earlier thread. 1000 fakes cost 3,072,000 credits, while an honest identity pays once and reclaims its bond. A rented-thread ring fails because sharing one thread groups all its clones, and a group burns every bond.
